title: A photograph as the ground, with a scrim that keeps the words readable
description: The other half of `backgroundGradient`, and the reason it is a separate port from `backgroundColor`. `backgroundImage` and `backgroundGradient` compose into ONE css background-image declaration with the gradient FIRST — so "var(--gradient-scrim)" paints over the picture and text laid on top stays legible whatever the photograph happens to be. That is the whole hero-over-an-image problem solved on one node, instead of an Image with an absolutely-positioned Group on top of it that an authoring model gets subtly wrong. `backgroundSize` cover crops the picture to the box; `backgroundPosition` decides what survives the crop; height is explicit because a band whose only content is a heading would otherwise collapse to the heading. `justifyContent` flex-end puts the copy at the foot of the frame, where the scrim is darkest — the scrim is a vertical gradient for exactly that reason. ⚠️ The shell inside it MUST carry `sizeMode: "contentHeight"`. Without it the shell is the runtime's 100%×100% default, becomes `flexGrow:100` in a column, fills the whole 520px band, and the band's `justifyContent` has nothing left to justify — the copy silently sits at the TOP with the scrim's dark end below it, empty. That is register V1, and it bit this recipe on its first render. `backgroundImage` here is `noodl_modules/starter-imagery/ground-city-dusk.webp`, one of the 44 CC0 photographs every project is created with — pick another by SUBJECT from `get_style_vocabulary`'s `imagery` block, or point it at your own asset or an https URL. Leaving it empty is not broken: the gradient alone is still a designed ground.
